 */

<file>
00001| ---
00002| title: after
00003| description: API Reference for the after function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| `after` allows you to schedule work to be executed after a response (or prerender) is finished. This is useful for tasks and other side effects that should not block the response, such as logging and analytics.
00007| 
00008| It can be used in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) (including [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata)), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), and [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).
00009| 
00010| The function accepts a callback that will be executed after the response (or prerender) is finished:
00011| 
00012| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00013| import { after } from 'next/server'
00014| // Custom logging function
00015| import { log } from '@/app/utils'
00016| 
00017| export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
00018|   after(() => {
00019|     // Execute after the layout is rendered and sent to the user
00020|     log()
00021|   })
00022|   return <>{children}</>
00023| }
00024| ```
00025| 
00026| ```jsx filename="app/layout.jsx" switcher
00027| import { after } from 'next/server'
00028| // Custom logging function
00029| import { log } from '@/app/utils'
00030| 
00031| export default function Layout({ children }) {
00032|   after(() => {
00033|     // Execute after the layout is rendered and sent to the user
00034|     log()
00035|   })
00036|   return <>{children}</>
00037| }
00038| ```
00039| 
00040| > **Good to know:** `after` is not a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) and calling it does not cause a route to become dynamic. If it's used within a static page, the callback will execute at build time, or whenever a page is revalidated.
00041| 
00042| ## Reference
00043| 
00044| ### Parameters
00045| 
00046| - A callback function which will be executed after the response (or prerender) is finished.
00047| 
00048| ### Duration
00049| 
00050| `after` will run for the platform's default or configured max duration of your route. If your platform supports it, you can configure the timeout limit using the [`maxDuration`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/maxDuration) route segment config.
00051| 
00052| ## Good to know
00053| 
00054| - `after` will be executed even if the response didn't complete successfully. Including when an error is thrown or when `notFound` or `redirect` is called.
00055| - In Server Components, you can use React [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to deduplicate functions called inside `after`. The callback reuses values already computed during the render. See [Reusing data with `React.cache`](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#reusing-data-with-reactcache).
00056| - `after` can be nested inside other `after` calls, for example, you can create utility functions that wrap `after` calls to add additional functionality.
00057| 
00058| ## Examples
00059| 
00060| ### With request APIs
00061| 
00062| Whether you can use request APIs like [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) inside `after` depends on where `after` is called from.
00063| 
00064| #### In Route Handlers and Server Functions
00065| 
00066| You can call `cookies` and `headers` directly inside the `after` callback when used in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) and [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). This is useful for logging activity after a mutation or API request. For example:
00067| 
00068| ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" highlight={2,10-16} switcher
00069| import { after } from 'next/server'
00070| import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers'
00071| import { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils'
00072| 
00073| export async function POST(request: Request) {
00074|   // Perform mutation
00075|   // ...
00076| 
00077|   // Log user activity for analytics
00078|   after(async () => {
00079|     const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown'
00080|     const sessionCookie =
00081|       (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous'
00082| 
00083|     logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent })
00084|   })
00085| 
00086|   return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), {
00087|     status: 200,
00088|     headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
00089|   })
00090| }
00091| ```
00092| 
00093| ```js filename="app/api/route.js" highlight={2,10-16} switcher
00094| import { after } from 'next/server'
00095| import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers'
00096| import { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils'
00097| 
00098| export async function POST(request) {

00100|   // ...
00101| 
00102|   // Log user activity for analytics
00103|   after(async () => {

`after` allows you to schedule work to be executed after a response (or prerender) is finished. This is useful for tasks and other side effects that should not block the response, such as logging and analytics.

It can be used in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) (including [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata)), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), and [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).
